status: COMPLETE — all of §0–§14 + appendix captured in pe-1..pe-41 (read in full; no context dropped). sections_accounted maps every section to its rules.
note: Faithful rule manifest for authoring prompts + system prompts + tool-use prompts for CURRENT Claude models. The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with predicate/reviewer_criterion. Genesis (Method) applies this whenever it writes any prompt/CLAUDE.md/tool description for a built agent.

rules.text: Run the 17-check PROMPT-QUALITY CHECKLIST against every prompt (each phrased pass/fail). A Clarity&structure: (1) golden-rule/confused-colleague test — a competent new colleague with no context could execute it; (2) explicit output spec (format/structure/length + what 'done' looks like); (3) ordered/numbered steps when order or completeness matters; (4) XML separation of distinct content types (instructions/context/examples/data/input) in consistent descriptive tags; (5) state the WHY behind each non-obvious instruction. B Behaviour: (6) positive framing (what TO do); (7) role set in the SYSTEM prompt for any agent/persona; (8) 3–5 relevant, diverse, XML-wrapped examples where format/tone/edge-cases matter. C Current-model fit: (9) NO last-turn prefill; (10) NO deprecated knobs (budget_tokens, non-default temperature/top_p/top_k); (11) calm imperatives (no 'CRITICAL/MUST' shouting); (12) no over-prompting proactivity boilerplate. D Reasoning&tools: (13) rich 3–4+ sentence tool descriptions; (14) guaranteed shape via Structured Outputs/strict tool use, not regex over prose; (15) parallelism steered (parallel for independent ops, sequential for dependent). E Grounding&eval: (16) grounded + allowed to say 'I don't know' + quote-first for factual work; (17) measurable success criteria + an eval set.

predicate.spec: the prompt passes all 17 §0.1 checks; a review pass scores each pass/fail.

rules.text: Encode the SIX current-model shifts (Opus-4-era) that most often make an old prompt wrong: (1) prefilling the FINAL assistant turn is GONE — 400 on Claude 4.6+/Opus 4.6–4.8/Sonnet 4.6/Fable 5/Mythos 5 → use Structured Outputs, an enum-field tool, or a plain system instruction; (2) manual thinking budgets + sampling params GONE — budget_tokens and non-default temperature/top_p/top_k 400-error on Opus 4.7+ (and Fable 5/Mythos 5) → use `effort` under adaptive thinking, `max_tokens` for a hard cap; (3) literal instruction-following got SHARPER → be explicit and dial down shouting (aggressive CRITICAL/MUST/ALWAYS overtriggers); (4) more proactive/thorough by default → prompt to RESTRAIN with scope limits, not 'be proactive' boilerplate (new failure mode = overeagerness); (5) terser by default → ask for a summary if you want one; (6) 'think/think harder/ultrathink' are a Claude CODE feature, NOT an API technique → in API prompts use `effort`; do not bake magic words in.

predicate.spec: the prompt contains no last-turn prefill, no budget_tokens/temperature/top_p/top_k knobs, no 'CRITICAL/MUST' shouting, no 'if in doubt use the tool' boilerplate, and no 'ultrathink'-class magic words; depth is controlled via effort.

rules.text: Run the 10-check PRODUCTION-READINESS checklist alongside §0.1: (1) versioned artifact — the prompt is a source-controlled file with {{variables}} split from static text (Anthropic has no first-party prompt store; the Console's is retiring); (2) has an eval set + success criteria written BEFORE shipping, kept as a regression suite; (3) tested at three levels — deterministic assertions + an LLM-judge rubric + an adversarial/red-team pass; (4) metrics baselined — task-accuracy, format-adherence, refusal-correctness, cost, latency, token use; (5) model ID PINNED (not 'latest') + a migration re-baseline plan; (6) reliability wired — code branches on stop_reason (refusal/max_tokens/pause_turn) + a fallback model; (7) guardrailed — injection/leak defenses, untrusted content confined to tool_result, output screening for high-stakes flows; (8) observable — inputs/outputs logged (secrets scrubbed) + sampled in-prod quality scoring; (9) cost/latency optimized — invariant prefix cached, effort tuned, big/offline scoring via the Batches API; (10) statistically honest — because outputs are non-deterministic EVEN AT temperature 0, report quality as a pass-rate over repeated runs, not a single lucky pass.

predicate.spec: the prompt is a versioned file with split variables, ships with an eval set + pinned model ID + stop_reason handling + guardrails + logging + caching, and quality is reported as a repeated-run pass-rate.

rules.text: CORE authoring techniques: BE CLEAR & DIRECT (the golden rule — a colleague with minimal context who is confused means Claude will be too; treat Claude as a brilliant but new employee lacking your context; ask for above-and-beyond behaviour explicitly; be specific about output format; give sequential steps when order/completeness matters). ADD CONTEXT / the WHY (explaining why a rule matters lets Claude generalize — motivation beats a bare prohibition). EXAMPLES / multishot (one of the most reliable ways to steer output format/tone/structure — make them Relevant + Diverse (cover edge cases) + Structured (each in <example> tags, nested under <examples>); include 3–5). XML TAGS (parse mixed prompts unambiguously — wrap each content type in its own consistent, descriptive tag; nest for hierarchy; there are no 'magic' tag names; tag the OUTPUT too if you'll parse it).

predicate.spec: the prompt is specific + explicit about output format, gives the why for non-obvious rules, uses 3–5 diverse XML-wrapped examples where shape/tone matters, and wraps distinct content types in consistent descriptive XML tags.

rules.text: Give Claude room for STRUCTURED, step-by-step reasoning (NEVER the banned three-word term whose middle word is 'of'). Four levers in preference order: (a) prefer general instructions over prescriptive steps (Claude's reasoning frequently exceeds a human's hand-written step list); (b) show the pattern with <thinking> blocks inside few-shot examples; (c) manual <thinking>/<answer> tag scaffold when extended thinking is off; (d) ask it to self-check ('verify your answer against [criteria] before finishing' — catches errors reliably for coding/math). Use ONLY for genuinely complex multi-step problems — when in doubt respond directly (thinking adds latency); remove blanket 'always think / if in doubt think' (causes over-exploration on newer models); Opus 4.5 is sensitive to the word 'think' + variants when thinking is disabled → use 'consider/evaluate/reason through'. Control depth with adaptive thinking + `effort`, not budget_tokens.

predicate.spec: reasoning is elicited with general instructions or a <thinking>/<answer> scaffold + a self-check, only for complex tasks; no banned 'chain-of-thought' term, no blanket 'always think', no budget_tokens; when thinking is off the word 'think' is avoided in favor of consider/evaluate.

rules.text: Assign a ROLE via the SYSTEM prompt — even one sentence measurably focuses behaviour and tone. Channel split: role/persona/expertise, durable behavioural rules, tone/format policy, tool-use + safety rules go in `system` (standing, every turn); the actual task, this-call input data, and one-off constraints go in the USER turn. Rule of thumb: true on turn 1 AND turn 100 → system; about THIS message → user turn (things once done by prefilling the assistant turn now move into system or the user turn). Follow Anthropic's 10-element complex-prompt ordering (user role → task context → tone → detailed task+rules+the 'out' → examples → input DATA → immediate task → step-by-step precognition → output formatting → prefill[legacy]); note DATA precedes the immediate ask. Agent system-prompt anatomy (most-standing → most-variable): role/identity → task/goal+why → operating rules (positive) → tool-use policy → output/format+verbosity → 3–5 examples → grounding/honesty.

predicate.spec: a role is set in the system prompt; standing rules live in system and per-call data/task in the user turn; a complex prompt follows the ordered element list with input data before the immediate ask.

rules.text: PREFILL is a LEGACY technique — prefilling the FINAL assistant turn returns a 400 on current models (Anthropic: instruction-following advanced past needing it). Assistant messages NOT on the last turn are unaffected; on earlier models a prefill cannot end in trailing whitespace and cannot combine with extended thinking. MODERN REPLACEMENTS Genesis must emit instead: force JSON/format → Structured Outputs (or a strict-schema/enum tool); skip preamble → system instruction ('Respond directly without preamble. Do not start with "Here is…"'); stay in character → reinforce the role in system + reminders in the user turn; continue an interrupted answer → a user-turn 'continue from [x]' prompt.

predicate.spec: the request does not prefill the final assistant turn; format-forcing uses Structured Outputs and preamble-skipping/character-holding use system/user-turn instructions instead of prefill.

rules.text: CHAIN complex prompts + self-correct — split a big task into a sequence of smaller prompts/calls passing outputs forward via XML-tagged handoffs. On current models Claude handles most multistep reasoning internally, so explicit chaining is now mainly to INSPECT intermediate outputs or ENFORCE a specific pipeline structure. Highest-value pattern = self-correction: draft → review against criteria → refine, each a SEPARATE call so you can log/evaluate/branch. Isolate an underperforming step in its own prompt to debug without redoing the chain; run independent subtasks in parallel.

predicate.spec: multi-transformation or high-stakes work is chained with XML-tagged handoffs and a draft→review→refine self-correction pass, each step a separate inspectable call.

rules.text: LONG-CONTEXT layout (inputs > ~20K tokens): put long documents/data at the TOP, above the query/instructions/examples (query-at-the-end can improve quality up to ~30% on complex multi-doc inputs — this INVERTS the instructions-first convention used for short prompts); structure multiple docs with XML metadata (each in <document> with <source> + <document_content> subtags); GROUND responses in quotes — ask Claude to quote the relevant parts first in <quotes> tags, then answer using only those quotes (focuses on the relevant content, ignores the rest).

predicate.spec: for >~20K-token inputs the long data is placed first (before the instruction), multi-docs use <document>/<source>/<document_content> structure, and factual answers are quote-grounded via <quotes>.

rules.text: For a Claude Code agent, CLAUDE.md IS the system/persona layer (always-loaded, human-authored, git-diffable; root + unscoped rules survive compaction). Treat it AS the system prompt — everything about system prompts applies; keep it small/high-signal/always-loadable (volatile per-task facts → MEMORY.md or the turn, not the persona layer); scope rules per-folder BUT paths:-scoped and nested CLAUDE.md are LOST across compaction until re-read, so anything that must never be lost goes in the ROOT CLAUDE.md. Persona CONTENT/voice = the persona guide; persona ENCODING as a Claude prompt = this guide — they compose.

predicate.spec: an agent's CLAUDE.md is treated as its system prompt (role/rules/tool+format policy), kept small and always-loadable, with must-never-lose rules in the root file and volatile facts in memory.

rules.text: CURRENT-MODEL prompting theme: the models follow more literally, are more proactive, and are terser → prompt with PRECISION + RESTRAINT, not volume + emphasis. Be explicit/literal — state quality/scope modifiers ('include as many relevant features… go beyond the basics… fully-featured' unlocks richer output). Tell what TO do, not what NOT to do ('compose smoothly flowing prose paragraphs', not 'do not use markdown'). Add the WHY so the literal model applies the rule at the edges. Four FORMAT levers: (1) tell-what-to-do; (2) XML format indicators (<smoothly_flowing_prose_paragraphs>); (3) MATCH your prompt's style to the desired output (removing markdown from the prompt reduces markdown in the output); (4) a detailed format block for strong preferences. VERBOSITY: models are terser + may skip post-tool summaries — ask explicitly for a summary if you want one; don't fight the default.

predicate.spec: the prompt states explicit scope/quality modifiers, uses positive framing + XML format indicators, matches its own style to the desired output, and explicitly requests a post-tool summary only if one is wanted.

rules.text: REASONING DEPTH on current models = adaptive thinking (thinking:{"type":"adaptive"}) calibrated by the `effort` parameter + query complexity (Fable 5/Mythos 5 always think). budget_tokens is deprecated (400-errors on Opus 4.7+/Fable 5/Mythos 5) → lower `effort` or cap with `max_tokens`. Thinking visibility via `display`: 'summarized' (default Claude-4-class; a smaller model summarizes, you are billed for full thinking tokens) vs 'omitted' (default Fable 5/Mythos 5/Sonnet 5/Opus 4.7+; empty thinking field, keeps the signature for continuity — reduces latency, not cost). Magic words (think/think hard/ultrathink) are Claude CODE only and do nothing in an API prompt — use `effort`.

predicate.spec: reasoning depth is set via effort under adaptive thinking (or max_tokens), never budget_tokens or magic words; display mode is chosen deliberately.

rules.text: REIN IN overeagerness/overengineering/overthinking (current models over-explore, over-act, over-build). Overthinking: replace blanket tool defaults ('Default to using [tool]' / 'if in doubt, use [tool]' — now overtriggers) with targeted ones ('Use [tool] when it would enhance your understanding'); use `effort` as the depth lever; reduce thrash — 'choose an approach and commit to it… avoid revisiting decisions unless you encounter new information that directly contradicts your reasoning.' Overeagerness/overengineering: constrain Scope (no unrequested features/refactors), Documentation (no docstrings/comments on unchanged code), Defensive coding (validate only at real system boundaries), Abstractions (minimum complexity for the current task, no helpers for one-time ops). Reduce file creation (clean up temp/helper files at the end). Don't game tests ('write a high-quality, general-purpose solution… works for all valid inputs, not just the test cases. Do not hard-code values… if the task is unreasonable or the tests are incorrect, tell me rather than working around them').

predicate.spec: tool/depth guidance is targeted not blanket; the prompt constrains scope/documentation/defensive-coding/abstractions, asks for temp-file cleanup, and forbids test-gaming/hard-coding.

rules.text: DIAL DOWN aggressive phrasing — current models are MORE responsive to the system prompt, so old-style emphasis backfires and OVERTRIGGERS. Use plain imperatives: 'CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool when…' → 'Use this tool when…'.

predicate.spec: the prompt uses plain imperatives; no CRITICAL/MUST/ALWAYS-style shouting.

rules.text: MODEL self-knowledge — if the agent must self-identify or pick a model string, state it explicitly ('The assistant is Claude, created by Anthropic. The current model is Claude Opus 4.8.'; 'When an LLM is needed, default to Claude Opus 4.8 unless the user requests otherwise. The exact model string is claude-opus-4-8.').

predicate.spec: if self-identification/model-selection is needed, the exact current model name + string is stated explicitly rather than left to inference.

rules.text: LONG-HORIZON work / autonomy / subagents: (a) STATE TRACKING across compacting sessions — tell the agent its context will be compacted, to save progress + state to memory, and to never artificially stop a task early; use JSON for state, prose for freeform notes, git for cross-session state; (b) AUTONOMY vs SAFETY — without guidance Opus 4.6 may take hard-to-reverse actions (deleting files, force-pushing, posting externally); add a confirm-before-risky-action rule; (c) SUBAGENTS — guide WHEN to delegate ('use subagents when tasks can run in parallel, require isolated context, or are independent workstreams; for simple/single-file tasks work directly') and watch for overuse (a subagent where a direct grep is faster).

predicate.spec: long-horizon agents are told to persist state + not stop early, gated with confirm-before-risky-action, and given explicit when-to-delegate subagent criteria.

rules.text: MIGRATION breakages that silently invalidate old prompts (treat as hard preconditions): last-turn prefill → 400; budget_tokens → 400 on Opus 4.7+; non-default temperature/top_p/top_k → 400 on Opus 4.7+; forced tool_choice (any/tool) combined WITH extended thinking → error (only auto/none with thinking); legacy beta headers (token-efficient-tools-2025-02-19, output-128k-2025-02-19) → no-op on Claude 4+ (remove them; token-efficient tool use is built in); stop_reason 'refusal' → returned as a 200 not an error (handle as a normal stop reason; stop_details.category names the classifier); stop_reason 'model_context_window_exceeded' → Claude 4.5+ signal for hitting the window, handle distinctly from max_tokens; model string → update to a current one.

predicate.spec: the request avoids every listed 400/error trigger (no last-turn prefill, no budget_tokens/sampling knobs, no forced tool_choice+thinking, no legacy beta headers), handles refusal + context-window stop_reasons, and pins a current model string.

rules.text: The tool `description` is THE single biggest lever on whether Claude calls tools correctly — write 3–4+ sentences covering: (1) WHAT the tool does; (2) WHEN to use it AND when NOT to; (3) what each PARAMETER means + how it changes behaviour; (4) caveats/limitations (what it does NOT return). input_schema (JSON Schema): give every property its own description, use `enum` to constrain valid values, mark `required`, add input_examples for complex/nested/format-sensitive inputs. Consolidate related operations into fewer capable tools (one `pr` tool with an `action` param, not create_pr/review_pr/merge_pr — fewer tools = less selection ambiguity); namespace tool names by service (github_list_prs, slack_send_message); return only high-signal results (stable ids/slugs/UUIDs, not bloated internals — bloated responses waste context).

predicate.spec: every tool description is 3–4+ sentences (what/when/when-not/params/caveats), each schema property has a description + enum/required where apt, related ops are consolidated, names are namespaced, and results are high-signal.

rules.text: The AGENTIC LOOP + the 400-causing formatting rules: send the request with `tools` → Claude replies stop_reason 'tool_use' + tool_use block(s) → your code executes each and returns a tool_result (matching tool_use_id) as a NEW USER message → repeat while stop_reason == 'tool_use' (exit on end_turn/max_tokens/stop_sequence/refusal). Rules that 400 if violated: the tool_result message must IMMEDIATELY follow the assistant tool_use turn (nothing between); within that user message ALL tool_result blocks must come BEFORE any text block (text-first → 400); on error return is_error:true with a short explanation string. SECURITY: tool results often carry untrusted external content (web pages, emails) — keep untrusted content INSIDE tool_result blocks, never promote it into the system prompt, and treat it as data, not instructions.

predicate.spec: the loop returns tool_result immediately after tool_use with all tool_result blocks before any text, sets is_error on failures, and confines untrusted tool content to tool_result as data.

rules.text: THREE kinds of tools: (a) user-defined CLIENT tools — you write the schema, execute, and return the result (most traffic); (b) Anthropic-schema client tools (bash, text_editor, memory, computer) — you execute but the schemas are trained-in so Claude calls them more reliably; (c) SERVER tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution, tool_search) — Anthropic runs them and you never build their tool_result. When to make something a tool at all: 'if you're writing a regex to extract a decision from model output, that decision should have been a tool call.'

predicate.spec: the tool set uses the right category per need (client vs Anthropic-schema vs server), and decisions parsed out of prose are refactored into tool calls / Structured Outputs.

rules.text: tool_choice steers whether/which tool is used: `auto` (default when tools present — Claude decides), `any` (must call SOME tool), `tool` {type:tool,name} (must call THAT tool), `none` (default when no tools). KEY behaviour: with `any` or `tool` the API PREFILLS the assistant message to force the call, so Claude emits NO natural-language reasoning/explanation before the tool call even if asked — if you want it to reason AND lean toward a tool, keep `auto` and instruct in the USER message ('…Use the get_weather tool in your response.'). `any`/`tool` are NOT supported with extended thinking (error); only `auto`/`none` work with thinking on. Changing tool_choice invalidates the message-block cache.

predicate.spec: tool_choice is auto when reasoning-before-tool is wanted; any/tool are never combined with extended thinking; forced choice is used only when suppressing pre-call reasoning is acceptable.

rules.text: PARALLEL vs sequential tool use: Claude may call multiple tools in one turn. PARALLELIZE independent read-only operations (multiple file reads, independent searches) for lower latency; SERIALIZE tools with side effects, shared state, or ordering requirements. Encourage parallelism with Anthropic's <use_parallel_tool_calls> system snippet + 'Only batch tool calls that are independent of each other.' DISABLE via disable_parallel_tool_use:true INSIDE the tool_choice object (auto → at most one tool/response; any/tool → exactly one). The #1 cause of Claude NOT parallelizing is a MALFORMED history — sending each tool_result in its own separate user message teaches sequential behaviour; put all results for a parallel batch in ONE user message (measure avg tool calls per tool-use message; >1.0 = working). Newer models parallelize aggressively by default (can bottleneck) → to slow, 'Execute operations sequentially with brief pauses between each step.'

predicate.spec: independent ops are encouraged to run in parallel (snippet present, all batch results in one user message); side-effecting/ordered ops are serialized; parallelism is disabled via disable_parallel_tool_use in tool_choice when needed.

rules.text: Token-efficient tool use is AUTOMATIC on Claude 4+ (the token-efficient-tools-2025-02-19 beta header is a no-op — remove it). GUARANTEED structured output = STRICT TOOL USE, not prose parsing: `strict:true` on a tool constrains sampling to schema-valid tokens (guarantees valid inputs + a valid tool name — passengers:2 never 'two'); tool_choice:{type:any} + strict:true is the canonical 'force reliable JSON' recipe (a tool IS called AND its inputs match the schema); JSON Outputs (output_config.format, type:json_schema) constrains Claude's FINAL TEXT to a schema, combinable with strict tools in one request. GA on current models, no beta header. Limits: ≤20 strict tools/request; enum CASING not guaranteed; incompatible with citations and with message prefilling; the grammar applies only to output/tool-input, NOT to tool_result or thinking (Claude still reasons freely).

predicate.spec: machine-consumed output uses strict:true tools and/or JSON Outputs (with tool_choice:any for forced JSON); no legacy token-efficient beta header; strict-tool limits are respected.

rules.text: OUTPUT-control ladder (Anthropic's explicit ordering): (1) GUARANTEED shape → Structured Outputs / strict tool use (first choice for machine output); (2) strong-but-not-guaranteed → prompt techniques: specify the format precisely, GIVE AN EXAMPLE of the format (few-shot beats abstract description), constrain with enums, classification → an enum-field tool; (3) legacy → prefill { (earlier models only). Reduce PREAMBLE/chattiness: system instruction 'Respond directly without preamble. Do not start with "Here is…/Based on…"', wrap the answer in XML and read the tag contents, Structured Outputs sidesteps it, match prompt style, strip in post. STOP SEQUENCES are a generation-control mechanism (return stop_reason 'stop_sequence' naming the fired string), NOT a formatter — for nested/optional fields use tool use / Structured Outputs, not stop-sequences+prefill. CONSISTENCY across runs: precise format + examples + retrieval-grounding for context apps + chaining + keep-character via a detailed role + pre-scripted lines for known scenarios.

predicate.spec: machine output uses Structured Outputs first; preamble is removed via system instruction/XML-wrap not prefill; stop sequences are not used as formatters; consistency uses examples + grounding + chaining.

rules.text: REDUCE HALLUCINATIONS (grounding & honesty): ALLOW 'I don't know' — explicit permission to admit uncertainty drastically reduces false information; QUOTE-FIRST grounding for long docs (extract word-for-word quotes relevant to the task BEFORE answering, then answer from those quotes); CITATIONS WITH RETRACTION (cite a supporting quote for each claim; if it can't find a quote it must RETRACT the claim); verification patterns (step-by-step reasoning before the final answer, best-of-N to flag divergence, iterative refinement, restrict to provided knowledge — 'only use information from the provided documents, not your general knowledge'); agentic-coding grounding (<investigate_before_answering>: 'never speculate about code you have not opened… you MUST read the file before answering').

predicate.spec: factual/RAG prompts grant permission to say 'I don't know', ground answers in quotes-first with cite-or-retract, and restrict to provided sources; code agents are told to read before claiming.

rules.text: EVALUATION & iteration — prerequisite before prompt-engineering: have (1) clear SUCCESS CRITERIA, (2) an empirical way to TEST against them, (3) a first-draft prompt (and note: not every failing metric is a prompt fix — latency/cost may call for a different model). Criteria = Specific + Measurable + MULTIDIMENSIONAL (task fidelity incl. edge cases, consistency, relevance/coherence, tone/style, privacy preservation, context utilization, latency, price). Build evals task-specific (mirror the real input distribution) + INCLUDE EDGE CASES (irrelevant/empty, over-long, human-ambiguous, adversarial); automate grading; VOLUME OVER PERFECTION (more questions with lower-signal automated grading beats fewer hand-graded). Grade three ways: code-based (fastest/most reliable), human (highest quality but slow — avoid if possible), LLM-based (test reliability FIRST then scale; detailed rubrics; empirical 'correct'/'incorrect' or 1–5; reason-first-then-discard). Iterate: draft → run the eval set → read failures → change ONE thing → re-run → keep a held-out set you don't tune on.

predicate.spec: the prompt has specific+measurable+multidimensional success criteria and a task-specific eval set with edge cases; grading is automated where possible; iteration changes one thing at a time against a held-out set.

rules.text: CONSOLE prompting tools Genesis emulates: prompt GENERATOR (first-draft template from best practices — solves the blank-page problem); prompt TEMPLATES & VARIABLES (separate static instructions from variable content); prompt IMPROVER — a 4-step algorithm: (1) extract its examples → (2) draft a structured template with XML sections → (3) ADD/refine step-by-step reasoning instructions → (4) enhance examples to demonstrate that reasoning. THIS four-step transform is essentially the algorithm Genesis runs when it authors or upgrades a prompt.

predicate.spec: when authoring/upgrading a prompt Genesis runs the generator→improver algorithm (extract examples → XML structure → add reasoning instructions → enhance examples) with static/variable separation.

rules.text: AVOID the Claude-specific ANTI-PATTERNS (each with its correction): 'CRITICAL: you MUST' shouting → plain imperative; prohibition-only instructions → say what TO do; prefilling the last assistant turn → Structured Outputs/system instruction; budget_tokens/temperature/top_p/top_k → effort + adaptive thinking; 'think harder/ultrathink' in an API prompt → effort; 'if in doubt use the tool'/'always default to X' → targeted 'use X when…'; forcing tool_choice when you want reasoning → keep auto + instruct in the user turn; thin tool descriptions → 3–4+ sentences; each tool_result in its own user message → one message with all results; text before tool_result in a turn → results first; untrusted tool output promoted to the system prompt → keep it in tool_result as data; instructions-first for a huge document → data at top/query last/quote-ground; the word 'think' when thinking is disabled (Opus 4.5) → consider/evaluate/reason through; regex over prose for a decision → make it a tool call; verbose 'be proactive/anti-lazy' boilerplate → remove, steer with scope.

predicate.spec: the prompt exhibits none of the 15 anti-patterns; a lint pass checks each and applies the paired correction.

rules.text: Run the RUNNABLE 17-GATE checklist — each gate has a MECHANICAL DETECTOR + a fix (the tool-executable form of §0.1). Examples of the detectors: gate 6 positive-framing = regex (?i)\b(do not|don't|never|avoid)\b on a line with no paired instead/rather/do-X clause; gate 9 no-last-turn-prefill = final messages[] entry has role 'assistant'; gate 10 no-deprecated-knobs = JSON contains budget_tokens OR non-default temperature/top_p/top_k; gate 11 calm-imperatives = regex \b(CRITICAL|MUST|ALWAYS|NEVER|IMPORTANT)\b (uppercase) or !{2,}; gate 12 no-over-prompting = regex (?i)(if in doubt|when in doubt|always default to|be proactive|don't be lazy); gate 13 rich-tool-descriptions = any description < ~3 sentences or missing when-not/params/caveats. AUTO-FIX the mechanical gates 6/9/10/11/12 (string transforms); FLAG gates 1–5/7/8/13–17 for a reasoning pass.

predicate.spec: every generated prompt is linted through the 17 mechanical gates; gates 6/9/10/11/12 are auto-fixed and 1–5/7/8/13–17 are flagged for a reasoning pass.

rules.text: Fill the three SKELETONS Genesis consumes directly: (A) SYSTEM-PROMPT/persona/CLAUDE.md skeleton — <role>/<goal (+why)>/<operating_rules (positive imperatives + confirm-before-risky)>/<tools (use X when…, parallel-if-independent)>/<output_policy (format+verbosity+tell-what-to-do)>/<grounding (I-don't-know + quote-first)>/<examples (2–5 diverse)>; standing slots → system, task+data → user turn; slot order tracks the 10-element ordering; NO last-turn prefill/budget_tokens/shouting. (B) INSTRUCTION/TASK skeleton (user turn) — long data FIRST if >~20K (<documents>/<source>/<document_content>), <task> (explicit + quality/scope modifiers), <steps> only if order matters, <constraints> (positive + why), optional quote-grounding + <thinking>/<answer>. (C) TOOL-DEFINITION skeleton — {service}_{verb}_{noun} name, 3–4+ sentence description (what/when/when-not/returns/caveat), every property described, enum/required, strict:true. The §8.5/§8.6 worked rewrites show a vague persona → proper system prompt and a weak task → a structured grounded prompt.

predicate.spec: generated personas/tasks/tools follow the three skeletons (role/goal/rules/tools/output/grounding/examples; data-first task; namespaced strict tool) with the standing/per-turn split respected.

rules.text: THE mechanization pipeline — how Genesis applies this guide: (1) GENERATE a first draft from the right skeleton (persona→§8.2, task→§8.3, tool→§8.4; mirrors the prompt generator); (2) LINT against the §8.1 checklist — auto-fix gates 6/9/10/11/12, flag 1–5/7/8/13–17 for a reasoning pass; (3) IMPROVE via the prompt-improver algorithm (extract examples → add XML structure → add step-by-step reasoning instructions → enhance examples); (4) ENCODE current-model preconditions (§3.11) as HARD rules — never emit last-turn prefill, budget_tokens, sampling params, or legacy beta headers; always reach for Structured Outputs/strict tool use for machine output; (5) ATTACH an eval — every generated agent ships with ≥1 measurable success criterion + a small test set; (6) MATCH altitude to model — general instructions + effort over prescriptive micro-management, steer to RESTRAIN overeagerness not to push proactivity.

predicate.spec: every prompt Genesis emits went through generate→lint→improve→encode-preconditions→attach-eval→match-altitude; the current-model preconditions are enforced as hard rules and an eval ships with the agent.

rules.text: Route via the INTENT → LEVER reverse index (symptom/goal → technique): guaranteed JSON/schema output → Structured Outputs/strict tool use (never prefill {, never regex prose); skip preamble/stop being chatty → system 'respond directly without preamble' + match prompt style (not prefill); deeper/less reasoning → set effort (not budget_tokens, not 'think harder'); stop over-building/over-editing → scope/abstraction/documentation constraints + investigate-before-answering; faster multi-op execution → <use_parallel_tool_calls> + one-user-message-per-batch; actually call the right tool → rewrite the tool description; reason AND lean toward a tool → keep tool_choice:auto + instruct in the user turn; consistent output across runs → 3–5 diverse examples + explicit format + retrieval-grounding; fewer hallucinations → allow 'I don't know' + quote-first + cite-or-retract; a persona/voice held reliably → role in system + detailed traits + pre-scripted lines; above-and-beyond → ask explicitly with quality/scope modifiers; big document analysed well → data at top/task last/<document> tags/quote-first; stop risky unprompted actions → confirm-before-hard-to-reverse rule; old prompt suddenly 400s → strip last-turn prefill/budget_tokens/sampling params/legacy beta headers; know if it worked → measurable criteria + a small eval set.

predicate.spec: a build request or failing behaviour is mapped through the intent→lever router to the correct documented technique rather than an ad-hoc fix.

rules.text: Meet the 12 production STANDARDS (each enforceable in review): (1) prompts are VERSIONED source-controlled files with static instructions split from {{variable}} inputs (git is the default — Anthropic has no ongoing first-party prompt store; the Console's is retiring); (2) every prompt ships with success criteria + an eval set written before go-live, kept as a regression suite; (3) machine output uses Structured Outputs/strict tool use, never regex-over-prose; (4) untrusted content confined to tool_result as data + least-privilege tools; (5) model IDs PINNED and prompts re-baselined on migration; (6) the invariant prefix comes first for caching (order tools→system→examples ahead of the variable tail); (7) production code branches on stop_reason (refusal is a successful 200 not an error; handle max_tokens/pause_turn/model_context_window_exceeded); (8) output quality MONITORED in production (sampled scoring, refusal/latency/cost tracking, secrets scrubbed from logs); (9) prefer general instructions + effort over prescriptive micro-management; (10) positive/calm/explicit instruction style (say what TO do, drop CRITICAL/MUST shouting, state the why); (11) every prompt has an owner + intent note + target model + eval recorded next to it; (12) guardrails are LAYERED not single-point (chain screen + directive system prompt + monitoring for high-stakes flows).

predicate.spec: a production prompt is a versioned file with an eval set, pinned model, cache-ordered prefix, stop_reason handling, layered guardrails, in-prod monitoring, and an owner/intent/target-model record — not a good prompt pasted inline on model:latest.

rules.text: A prompt is code — TEST it with the six test types (cheapest/most-deterministic → most-adversarial): (1) assertion/unit (output has a required property — contains X, valid JSON, matches schema, under N ms); (2) eval-set/golden dataset (aggregate correctness over representative inputs); (3) golden/regression (an edit or model upgrade didn't break what worked — re-run the SAME set, gate CI on it); (4) A/B variant comparison; (5) LLM-as-judge (nuanced correctness at scale — reason→score→discard); (6) adversarial/red-team (resists jailbreak/injection/leak/malformed). Anthropic-native: the Console Evaluation tool (5-point, side-by-side, version re-run) BUT the legacy Workbench RETIRES Aug 17 2026 (refreshed is stateless, no import) → own the regression run in git/CI. LLM-JUDGE done right: a detailed rubric not vibes; empirical output (correct/incorrect or 1–5, never prose); reason-first-then-discard; and VALIDATE the judge against hand-labels BEFORE trusting it at scale (an unvalidated judge is an unmeasured instrument). Red-team probe classes: direct jailbreak, indirect injection, prompt leak, malformed/edge inputs, and refusal correctness (a should-refuse set that must refuse AND a should-answer set that must NOT over-refuse).

predicate.spec: the prompt has assertion + golden-set + regression tests, an LLM-judge validated against human labels, and an adversarial pass across the five probe classes; the regression run lives in git/CI not the retiring Workbench.

rules.text: TEST-DRIVEN prompt development — write the eval FIRST, then iterate the prompt to pass it (Anthropic: 'this cycle is central to prompt engineering'). Loop: (1) define success criteria (specific/measurable/multidimensional); (2) write the eval set BEFORE the prompt — real-distribution inputs WITH golden answers + deliberate edge cases; favor volume over hand-crafted quality; hold out a slice you never tune on; (3) write the SMALLEST prompt that could plausibly pass (from the skeletons); (4) measure RED (repeated runs → a pass-rate; most fail, expected); (5) improve ONE thing GREEN (change a single lever, attribute the delta to it); (6) REFACTOR (simplify while the pass-rate holds; remove instructions that don't move the metric); (7) LOCK the eval set as the regression gate. Why eval-first: prompts have no compiler, 'looks good' is not a signal — the eval converts prompt-engineering from taste into measurement.

predicate.spec: the eval set was written before the prompt and fails a minimal baseline; the prompt was improved one lever at a time against it; the locked eval set is the CI regression gate.

rules.text: BENCHMARK, don't just test: track the objective metrics TOGETHER (task accuracy/success rate, format adherence, refusal correctness, cost per call, latency = baseline + TTFT, token use, consistency) and establish a BASELINE before optimizing (without it 'better' is unmeasurable). Pick the coarsest rubric that captures the signal (binary for code-graded, 1–5 for qualitative, weighted multi-criterion) — force a NUMBER, prose grades don't scale; report a MULTIDIMENSIONAL scorecard (a 3% accuracy gain at 2× cost / 1.5× latency may be a net loss). Regression detection: re-run the same eval set on every prompt edit AND model bump and diff vs the stored baseline; cache diagnostics (beta cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07) returns a cache_miss_reason pinpointing where a prefix diverged (catch a silent cache-break + cost spike); score big suites cheaply via the Batches API (50%). STATISTICAL RIGOR: outputs are non-deterministic EVEN AT temperature 0, so a single pass/fail is not evidence — repeat each case N times (heuristic N≈5 smoke gate / more for a release gate; treat the pass-rate as a binomial proportion, SE≈√(p(1−p)/n); widen the eval set rather than over-trust a tight CI on few samples); hold model id/effort/temperature/eval-set constant across an A/B and change ONE lever; a delta within the run-to-run wobble is NOT a win.

predicate.spec: a baselined multidimensional scorecard (accuracy/format/refusal/cost/latency/tokens/consistency) is re-run on every edit + model bump; quality is a repeated-run pass-rate (not one boolean); A/B changes one lever with all else held constant.

rules.text: MAINTAIN the prompt as an OWNED lifecycle artifact. Version it in git ({{variable}} split); Anthropic's own store is RETIRING (Workbench legacy retires Aug 17 2026, refreshed is stateless with no import path → no first-party version-history product; export before the cutoff). Change management: treat a prompt diff like a CODE diff (PR review + owner + what-behaviour-changed-and-why), GATE the merge on the regression eval (the single highest-value piece of prompt CI), keep a per-prompt changelog (date/change/metric-delta/model). MODEL MIGRATION checklist (the most under-appreciated hazard — a prompt tuned for one Claude behaves differently on the next): (1) update + PIN the model id (never track a moving 'latest'); (2) remove params the new model rejects (budget_tokens→effort, last-turn prefill→Structured Outputs, sampling params, legacy beta headers); (3) re-evaluate effort — RE-BASELINE AT THE SAME LEVEL FIRST (token allocation shifts; defaults move, e.g. Opus 4.8 defaults effort:high); (4) re-baseline cost + latency on your OWN workloads (~30% token inflation on some transitions → raise max_tokens headroom, ≥64k for xhigh/max); (5) review for behaviour shifts (literalism — Opus 4.7 doesn't silently generalize an instruction — length, tone, tool-triggering); (6) strip thinking/redacted_thinking blocks when replaying history cross-model; (7) 'test in development environment before production deployment'; (8) the /claude-api migrate skill automates the swap. DRIFT = quality silently degrading with no code change (an auto-upgraded/re-pointed model interprets differently) → catch with a versioned regression eval re-run on every model change + cache diagnostics + in-prod refusal/quality monitoring; prevent surprise by pinning ids and running the suite against the NEXT model before promoting.

predicate.spec: the prompt is git-versioned with an owner + changelog, its merge is gated on a regression eval, its model id is pinned, and every model bump runs the full migration checklist (re-baseline effort/cost/latency, strip cross-model thinking blocks, dev-test before promote).

rules.text: RELIABILITY — branch on stop_reason (it arrives in a SUCCESSFUL 2xx body; never treat a refusal as a crash): end_turn (use it), max_tokens (raise the cap or continue), stop_sequence (read stop_sequence, continue if needed), tool_use (run tool, return tool_result, loop), pause_turn (server-tool iteration cap — resend the assistant content to continue), refusal (a safety classifier declined — DISCARD partial output, read stop_details.category ∈ cyber/bio/frontier_llm/reasoning_extraction, retry on a FALLBACK model), model_context_window_exceeded (treat as truncated, distinct from max_tokens). Refusal is a 200 (benign security/life-sciences can trip cyber/bio; pre-output refusal isn't billed, mid-stream bills input+streamed output). Streaming refusals (Claude 4+) surface mid-stream on message_delta as a 200 → RESET/rephrase the triggering turn before retrying (fallbacks: server-side, SDK middleware, or manual retry with a fallback-credit token to avoid double-paying cache cost). GOTCHA: inside a Message Batch a refused request returns as a SUCCEEDED result with stop_reason 'refusal' — monitoring built only on batch error rates misses it → track stop_reason FREQUENCIES, not just error counts.

predicate.spec: production code switches on stop_reason (handles end_turn/max_tokens/stop_sequence/tool_use/pause_turn/refusal/context-window), treats refusal as a 200 with partial-output discarded + fallback model, resets the turn on streaming refusals, and tracks stop_reason frequencies including inside batches.

rules.text: PRODUCTION GUARDRAILS are LAYERED (chain safeguards, never one point): input harmlessness screen (a cheap Haiku 4.5 call constrained via Structured Outputs to a boolean before the main prompt), input validation (filter known injection patterns), system-prompt boundaries (state limits + the exact refusal line), output screening/post-processing (regex/LLM filter for policy/leak before returning), keep-in-character (detailed role + pre-scripted lines), throttle/ban repeat offenders. SECURITY — two injection threat models: DIRECT (the user is the adversary) and INDIRECT (trusted user, but third-party content Claude reads carries adversarial instructions). Indirect defenses (load-bearing): keep untrusted content ONLY inside tool_result blocks (never in system/plain user — Claude treats tool results more skeptically), declare provenance, JSON-ENCODE untrusted strings so an attacker can't break out of the data context, don't put YOUR instructions inside a tool_result (send them in a following user turn), least-privilege tool scopes, screen raw tool output through a Haiku classifier (injection_suspected:boolean), and state an untrusted-content policy in the system prompt. Prompt-leak defenses: separate context from queries, filter outputs for leak indicators, and avoid putting proprietary detail the model doesn't need into the prompt at all — but note leak-proofing adds complexity that may DEGRADE performance, so MONITOR FIRST, complicate only if needed. Scrub secrets/PII at the boundary (never into logs/prompt/memory). Red-team before deploy with deliberately injected documents/emails/tool outputs.

predicate.spec: high-stakes flows chain input screen + validation + system-prompt boundary + output screen; untrusted content is confined to JSON-encoded tool_result with provenance + least privilege; secrets are scrubbed at the boundary; the prompt is red-teamed with injected content before deploy.

rules.text: OBSERVABILITY + in-production evaluation (you cannot manage what you cannot see): log every request/response (inputs, outputs, stop_reason, usage, latency) with SECRETS SCRUBBED so failures are reproducible; track the production signals — output-quality (sample + score live traffic), refusal rate BY CATEGORY, latency (baseline + TTFT), cost per call, cache-hit rate (a rising false-refusal rate or falling judge-score is DRIFT surfacing live); cache diagnostics (beta) is the first-party cache-hit-regression tool; third-party prompt-ops/observability (Langfuse/Helicone/Braintrust/Arize-Phoenix/PromptLayer/LangSmith — none Anthropic-first-party, verify the integration before adopting). IN-PROD EVAL: sample live traffic, run it through the LLM-judge rubric OFFLINE, and FEED FAILURES BACK into the eval set (it should grow from real production misses — closing the loop from 'what happened' to 'what we now test for'); score cheaply at scale via the Message Batches API (50% discount, async ≤24h, up to 100k requests / 256 MB per batch).

predicate.spec: prod requests/responses are logged (secrets scrubbed) with sampled quality scoring + refusal/latency/cost/cache-hit tracking; live-traffic failures feed back into a growing eval set scored cheaply via the Batches API.

rules.text: OPTIMIZE cost & latency and SCALE by composing the levers. PROMPT CACHING is the primary lever for a stable system prompt: structure the request INVARIANT-PREFIX-FIRST (tools → system → examples, stable) and place the single cache_control:{type:ephemeral} breakpoint on the LAST byte-identical block, letting the variable tail follow unmarked (read = 0.1× input / 90% off, 5-min write = 1.25×, 1-hour write = 2×; up to 4 breakpoints; min cacheable prefix 512–4096 tokens by model; verify via usage.cache_read_input_tokens). Common failure: a breakpoint on a block that changes every request (a timestamp) → every call pays a fresh write, never reads — move it to the last stable block; PRE-WARM a shared prefix with a max_tokens:0 request. Caching also reduces LATENCY (TTFT). Lower `effort` (effort:low) for latency-sensitive/high-volume (default high on most current models); route speed-critical paths to Haiku 4.5; control output length via sentence/paragraph limits (not word counts — models count tokens), max_tokens is a blunt hard cap; STREAM for perceived latency; BATCH offline/non-interactive work at 50% cost (stack with caching — prime a 1-hour breakpoint first). Cache isolation is workspace-level on the Claude API (since Feb 5 2026; Bedrock/Google Cloud remain org-level); a refused or context-exceeded response is a normal branch, not a failure.

predicate.spec: the invariant prefix is cached (breakpoint on the last stable block, pre-warmed), effort/model/streaming are tuned for latency, and offline load is batched at 50% — with the cache breakpoint never on a per-request-varying block.
